[[Taraba F.C.|Taraba]] (4) | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2014 Nigeria Professional Football League|2014]] | nextseason = [[2016 Nigeria Professional Football League|2016]] | updated = 16 November 2015 }} The '''2015 Nigeria Professional Football League''' (referred to as the Nigerian [[Globacom|Glo]] premier league for sponsorship reasons) is the 44th season of the [[Nigeria Premier League]], the top Nigerian professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1972. It is also the 25th season since the league was rebranded as the "Professional League." [[Enyimba F.C.|Enyimba]] won their seventh league title and first since the [[2009–10 Nigeria Premier League|2009–10 season]]. They clinched with a week to go in the season with a scoreless draw with [[Warri Wolves F.C.|Warri Wolves]], who were six points behind. Warri Wolves finished in second place, four points behind Enyimba, and both will represent Nigeria in the [[2016 CAF Champions League]]. [[Nasarawa United F.C.|Nasarawa United]] placed third and qualified for the [[2016 CAF Confederation Cup]]. [[Bayelsa United F.C.|Bayelsa United]], [[Kwara United F.C.|Kwara United]], [[Sharks F.C.|Sharks]] and [[Taraba F.C.|Taraba]] each finished in the bottom four and will be relegated to the [[Nigeria National League]] for 2016. [[Akwa United F.C.|Akwa United]] escaped relegation, pulling out of the bottom four with a 1-0 win over [[Lobi Stars F.C.|Lobi Stars]] in their final match of the season. ==Clubs== A total of 20 teams will contest the league including 16 teams from the [[2014 Nigeria Premier League|previous season]] and four teams promoted from the [[Nigeria National League]]. In June, the league forced several clubs to find new venues for Matchdays 12 and 13 while they make mandatory upgrades to their home grounds.{{cite web |url=http://www.npfl.ng/index.php/news-features/club-news/946-seven-clubs-settle-for-new-homes-lmc-awaits-giwa-nasarawa |title=Seven clubs settle for new homes, LMC awaits Giwa, Nasarawa |website=www.npfl.ng |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150621214302/http://www.npfl.ng/index.php/news-features/club-news/946-seven-clubs-settle-for-new-homes-lmc-awaits-giwa-nasarawa |archive-date=21 June 2015 |url-status=dead}} In August, Kano Pillars' 12-year undefeated streak at home came to an end in a 2-1 loss to Nasarawa United.[https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34035720Nigerian Premier League side's unbeaten record ends]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} == References == {{reflist}} *http://npfl.ng/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025165319/http://npfl.ng/ |date=2015-10-25 }} {{Nigeria Premier League Seasons}} {{2015 in African football (CAF)}} [[Category:Nigeria Professional Football League seasons]] [[Category:2015 in Nigerian football|1]] [[Category:2015 in African association football leagues|Nigeria]]
